idea: The user's rule since 2026-11-26: Kokpit 360 shows how to build an airplane from scratch, one part per episode, in high-quality 3D made with Blender (engine/kokpit_blender). We build ONE two-seat light aircraft (a generic high-performance trainer shape, no brand) and the same model grows from episode to episode, so viewers come back for the next part.
how_to_use: Take the FIRST episode without used_by (they are in build order; never skip ahead unless the user asks).
Title/series tag: 'Sıfırdan Uçak #<n>' on the first frame (compose.py ass PROJECT 'SIFIRDAN UÇAK #<n>'), in the title and in the caption.
Build the scene with kb.light_aircraft(stage=<stage>) so every part made in earlier episodes is already there; animate THIS episode's part (fly_in / scale_in / glow / hinge / flow_lines).

The facts below are a starting point. Confirm every number with 2 reliable web sources (FAA handbooks on faa.gov, manufacturer data, NASA/Glenn, university aero pages, EAA). Cut a fact that fails. Never copy any source's wording.
Max 3 facts, 25-35 s, hook in the first second, end with 'Sıradaki parça: <next episode's part>. Takip et.' (the next part is a real forward reference).
After publishing set used_by=<slug> on the episode and commit this file to engine/ with the video.
safety_note: Education only. Never present the video as building instructions for a real aircraft to fly. Where it fits, the description says: 'Eğitim amaçlıdır. Gerçek bir uçak yapımı SHGM/FAA onayı ve uzman denetimi gerektirir.' No crash footage, no accidents used for views (Meta + YouTube policy, PLAYBOOK ethics).

episodes.title_tr: Uçak yapmaya kanattan değil, teraziden başlanır
episodes.hook: Uçak yapmaya kanatla başlanmaz… önce bir terazi lazım.
facts: A designer first fixes the maximum takeoff weight; every part gets a weight budget (FAA Pilot's Handbook of Aeronautical Knowledge, weight & balance chapter).
Example to verify: a two-seat trainer like the Cessna 152 has a max takeoff weight around 757 kg (1,670 lb).
Every extra kilogram needs more lift, so more wing area or more speed.
episodes.visual: blueprint outline of the aircraft drawn by glowing lines on the studio floor, a balance scale icon, weight numbers counting up

episodes.hook: Bu şekil bir damla değil… uçağı havada tutan sır bu kesitte.
facts: The cross-section is the airfoil; many light trainers use the NACA 2412 family (verify for Cessna 152).
The curved, angled shape turns the passing air downward; the air pushes the wing up in return (NASA Glenn 'lift' pages).
Angle of attack matters more than the curve: tilt it too far and the flow separates (stall).
episodes.visual: kb.airfoil_slab big teal airfoil, kb.flow_lines over and under it, downwash arrows, angle-of-attack tilt

episodes.hook: Uçuşta kanat yukarı doğru eğilir… onu kırılmaktan kurtaran tek bir parça var.
facts: The main spar carries the bending load of the wing like a beam (FAA Aviation Maintenance Technician Handbook - Airframe).
Normal-category aircraft are designed for a limit load factor of +3.8 g, utility +4.4 g (14 CFR 23 - verify current wording).
The spar caps (top and bottom) take the most stress; the web between them keeps them apart.
episodes.visual: spar flies in, glows orange; wing bends upward with an exaggerated arrow, stress glow on top/bottom caps

episodes.hook: Kanadın içinde bir balık kılçığı var.
facts: Ribs give the wing its airfoil shape and pass air loads from the skin to the spar (FAA AMT Airframe handbook).
Ribs have lightening holes to save weight.
Count of ribs depends on the design - give a real example only if a source states it.
episodes.visual: 14 ribs fly in one by one onto the spar (kb.fly_in stagger), camera slides along the span

episodes.hook: Bu ince alüminyum sadece bir örtü değil… yükü o taşıyor.
facts: Modern metal wings use 'stressed skin': the skin carries part of the load (FAA AMT Airframe handbook).
Typical light-aircraft skin is thin aluminium alloy such as 2024-T3 (verify thickness range with 2 sources).
Early aircraft (Wright Flyer) used fabric over a wooden frame.
episodes.visual: wing skin fades in over ribs (kb.fade), light sweeps across, then a cut-away shows skeleton under skin

episodes.title_tr: Uçaklar neden kaynak değil perçinle birleşir?
episodes.hook: Bu uçakta tek bir kaynak yok… hepsi perçin.
facts: Heat-treated aluminium alloys like 2024-T3 lose strength when welded, so they are riveted (FAA AMT handbook).
Rivets spread the load across many points and are easy to inspect.
A large airliner has very many rivets - only state a number with 2 sources.
episodes.visual: rows of tiny glowing rivet dots appear along the skin seams, close-up with shallow focus

episodes.hook: Uçak yana yatarken iki kanadın ucu ters yöne hareket eder.
facts: Ailerons on the outer trailing edge move in opposite directions (FAA PHAK flight controls).
The up-going aileron's wing gets more lift, the other less, so the aircraft rolls.
Adverse yaw: the rising wing also gets more drag, so pilots add rudder.
episodes.visual: aileron cut out of each wing tip, kb.hinge opposite directions, roll arrow

episodes.hook: İnişe geçerken kanat kendini büyütür.
facts: Flaps on the inner trailing edge increase lift and drag so the aircraft can fly slower (FAA PHAK).
That allows a steeper, slower approach and a shorter landing.
Types: plain, split, slotted, Fowler (Fowler also adds wing area).
episodes.visual: flaps extend down and back (hinge + slide), flow lines bend more downward

episodes.hook: Bu gövde bir yumurta kabuğu gibi çalışıyor.
facts: Most metal aircraft are semi-monocoque: frames (formers) + stringers + stressed skin (FAA AMT Airframe).
Frames keep the shape, stringers stop the skin from buckling.
Monocoque means the skin alone carries the load - like an egg shell.
episodes.visual: frames scale in front to back, then stringers draw along them; orbit shot

episodes.title_tr: Gövde kaplaması neden bu kadar ince?
episodes.hook: Bu gövdenin duvarı bir madeni paradan ince.
facts: Verify typical fuselage skin thickness of light aircraft (mm) with 2 sources before using a number.
Thin skin is enough because the shape and stringers stabilise it.
Weight saved in structure becomes payload or fuel.
episodes.visual: fuselage skin fades in panel by panel, coin for scale

episodes.hook: Uçağın kuyruğu onu yukarı değil, aşağı doğru iter.
facts: On a conventional aircraft the centre of gravity is ahead of the centre of lift, so the tail usually pushes down to balance (FAA PHAK stability).
The elevator changes the tail's force to pitch the nose up or down.
This 'tail-down force' makes the aircraft stable in pitch.
episodes.visual: horizontal stabiliser flies in, see-saw balance arrows (lift up, weight down, tail down)

episodes.title_tr: Uçakta direksiyon yok, peki nasıl döner?
episodes.hook: Uçak, sadece dikey kuyrukla dönmez.
facts: The vertical stabiliser keeps the nose pointing into the airflow like a weather vane (FAA PHAK).
The rudder yaws the nose; turns are made by banking with the ailerons, rudder coordinates.
Pilots control the rudder with their feet (pedals).
episodes.visual: fin rises up, rudder hinges left/right, weather-vane arrow

episodes.hook: Bu uçağı tek bir noktadan dengeleyebilirsin.
facts: Every aircraft has a certified centre-of-gravity range (FAA Weight & Balance Handbook).
CG too far aft makes the aircraft unstable and hard to recover from a stall.
That is why pilots calculate weight and balance before every flight.
episodes.visual: the model balanced on a glowing pin, CG marker slides fore/aft, nose tips

episodes.title_tr: Küçük uçağın motoru araba motoruna benzer mi?
episodes.hook: Bu motorun silindirleri yan yatmış… ve bunun bir sebebi var.
facts: Many light aircraft use air-cooled horizontally-opposed (boxer) piston engines (FAA PHAK powerplant chapter).
Flat layout = low frontal area and good air cooling.
They usually have dual ignition: two spark plugs per cylinder, two magnetos, for safety.
episodes.visual: engine block assembles (cylinders fly in from the sides), glow on spark plugs

episodes.hook: Pervane düz değil… ucuna doğru burulur.
facts: A propeller blade is a rotating wing; it makes thrust like a wing makes lift (FAA PHAK).
The tip moves much faster than the root, so the blade is twisted to keep a good angle of attack along its length.
Tip speed is kept below the speed of sound for efficiency and noise (verify).
episodes.visual: propeller spins (kb.spin), slow-motion, flow lines through the disc, twist highlighted root vs tip

episodes.hook: Bu uçağın yakıtı gövdede değil, kanatlarda.
facts: Light aircraft usually carry fuel in wing tanks (FAA PHAK fuel systems).
High-wing aircraft can feed by gravity; low-wing need fuel pumps.
Fuel in the wings also reduces wing root bending in flight (bending relief).
episodes.visual: wing turns semi-transparent, glowing fuel volume fills, lines run to the engine

episodes.title_tr: Üç teker mi, kuyruk tekeri mi?
episodes.hook: Bu uçağın iniş takımı bir yay gibi esner.
facts: Tricycle gear (nose wheel) is easier to handle on the ground than a tailwheel (FAA Airplane Flying Handbook).
Many light aircraft use spring-steel or composite leg gear that absorbs the landing.
Retractable gear reduces drag but adds weight and complexity.
episodes.visual: legs + wheels fly in, a landing bounce with the legs flexing

episodes.hook: Klasik bir kokpitte her pilotun ezbere bildiği altı saat var.
facts: The 'six-pack': airspeed, attitude, altimeter, turn coordinator, heading, vertical speed (FAA PHAK flight instruments).
Three of them use air pressure (pitot-static), three use gyroscopes.
Modern glass cockpits show the same six on screens.
episodes.visual: canopy fades in, camera flies into the cabin, six glowing round gauges pop in

episodes.title_tr: Uçak hızını küçük bir boru ile ölçer
episodes.hook: Uçağın hız göstergesi aslında küçük bir boruya bağlı.
facts: The pitot tube measures ram air pressure; the static port measures still air pressure (FAA PHAK).
Their difference gives the indicated airspeed.
A blocked pitot tube gives false airspeed - pitot heat prevents icing.
episodes.visual: close-up of a pitot tube under the wing, flow lines enter, pressure glow to the gauge

episodes.title_tr: Sıfırdan yapılan uçak ilk kez nasıl uçar?
episodes.hook: Uçak bitti… ama hemen uçmuyor.
facts: Amateur-built aircraft need an airworthiness inspection and a flight-test period before carrying passengers (FAA experimental amateur-built rules; in Turkey SHGM).
First flights are done by an experienced test pilot near the airfield.
Tests start with taxi and high-speed taxi runs before lift-off.
episodes.visual: finished aircraft rolls across the blueprint floor, wheels spin, lifts off; series recap montage
